records.source: וַיֵּצְאוּ֮ כָּל־בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵל֒ וַתִּקָּהֵ֨ל הָעֵדָ֜ה כְּאִ֣ישׁ אֶחָ֗ד לְמִדָּן֙ וְעַד־בְּאֵ֣ר שֶׁ֔בַע וְאֶ֖רֶץ הַגִּלְעָ֑ד אֶל־יְהוָ֖ה הַמִּצְפָּֽה׃
records.gloss: And went out all [the] sons of Israel, and was assembled the congregation as one man, from Dan and to Beersheba and [the] land of the Gilead, to Yahweh [at] the Mizpah.
pieces: Then all the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} came out, from Dan to Beersheba and from the land of Gilead, and the congregation gathered as one before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} at Mizpah.

L.1: And all the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel went out, and the congregation assembled as one man, from Dan to Beersheba, and the land of Gilead, to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} at Mizpah.

R.1: Then all the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} came together, from Dan in the far north to Beersheba in the far south, and from the land of Gilead east of the Jordan. The whole community met as one before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} at Mizpah.

decisions.choice: from Dan to Beersheba, and Gilead: the whole of Israel, north, south and east of the Jordan
decisions.reason: Dan was the northernmost town (18:29) and Beersheba the southernmost, so "from Dan to Beersheba" means the whole land west of the Jordan (1 Samuel 3:20). Gilead adds the tribes east of the Jordan. Every part of Israel answered the summons the Levite sent out (19:29-30).

decisions.choice: as one man: all together, with one purpose
decisions.reason: The phrase pictures the whole people acting as if they were a single person. It comes again in verses 8 and 11, and it stresses how united the tribes were against Benjamin.

decisions.choice: to the LORD at Mizpah: a gathering held in the LORD's presence
decisions.reason: Mizpah ("lookout") was a town in Benjamin's land, north of Jerusalem, where Israel later gathered before the LORD again (1 Samuel 7:5-6; 10:17). To assemble "to the LORD" means the meeting was held as before God, not only as a council of the tribes.

decisions.choice: in the far north ... in the far south ... east of the Jordan
decisions.reason: Readable says where the places lay, so the reader sees that the phrase means the whole country (m1).

records.heading: The tribes gather at Mizpah

records.source: וַיִּֽתְיַצְּב֞וּ פִּנּ֣וֹת כָּל־הָעָ֗ם כֹּ֚ל שִׁבְטֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל בִּקְהַ֖ל עַ֣ם הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים אַרְבַּ֨ע מֵא֥וֹת אֶ֛לֶף אִ֥ישׁ רַגְלִ֖י שֹׁ֥לֵֽף חָֽרֶב׃פ
records.gloss: And presented themselves [the] corners of all the people, all [the] tribes of Israel, in [the] assembly of [the] people of the God: four hundred thousand man on foot drawing [the] sword.
pieces: The leaders of the whole people, of all the tribes of Israel, took their places in the assembly of the people of God: 400,000 foot soldiers armed with swords.

L.2: And the corners of all the people, all the tribes of Israel, presented themselves in the assembly of the people of God: 400,000 men on foot drawing [the] sword.

R.2: The leaders of all the tribes of Israel took their places in the meeting of God's people. There were 400,000 soldiers on foot, all armed with swords.

decisions.choice: the corners: the leaders
decisions.reason: The word means "corners", as the cornerstones that hold up a building. Used of people it means the chief men who hold up the people (1 Samuel 14:38; Isaiah 19:13).

decisions.choice: 400,000: a very large army; the word for "thousand" may also name a unit
decisions.reason: As noted at Numbers 1, the word for "thousand" can also be used of a military or clan unit, which would give a much smaller number of men. The same question applies to every large number in this chapter.

decisions.choice: drawing the sword: armed fighting men
decisions.reason: A man "drawing the sword" is one fit and armed to fight. The phrase recurs through the chapter (verses 15, 17, 25, 35, 46) as the way the armies are counted.
Numbers above ninety-nine are written in numerals.

decisions.choice: leaders
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the meaning of "corners" (m1); Literal keeps the picture.

records.source: וַֽיִּשְׁמְעוּ֙ בְּנֵ֣י בִנְיָמִ֔ן כִּֽי־עָל֥וּ בְנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל הַמִּצְפָּ֑ה וַיֹּֽאמְרוּ֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל דַּבְּר֕וּ אֵיכָ֥ה נִהְיְתָ֖ה הָרָעָ֥ה הַזֹּֽאת׃
records.gloss: And heard [the] sons of Benjamin that had gone up [the] sons of Israel [to] the Mizpah. And said [the] sons of Israel, Speak: how did happen the evil the this?
pieces: The Benjaminites heard that the Israelites had gone up to Mizpah. Then the Israelites said, "Tell us how this evil thing happened."

L.3: And the sons of Benjamin heard that the sons of Israel had gone up to Mizpah. And the sons of Israel said, "Speak: how did this evil happen?"

R.3: The men of Benjamin heard that the rest of the Israelites had gone up to Mizpah. The Israelites said, "Tell us how this terrible crime happened."

decisions.choice: Benjamin heard: the tribe knew of the gathering but did not come
decisions.reason: The verse sets Benjamin apart from the rest at the start. They heard of the assembly, yet they are not among those who came, and so the matter is heard without them.

decisions.choice: this evil: this wicked deed
decisions.reason: The word means evil or wickedness, here a crime. It is the word the tribes use again in verses 12 and 13, where they ask Benjamin to remove "the evil" from Israel.

decisions.choice: the sons of Benjamin (L); the Benjaminites (B); the men of Benjamin (R)
decisions.reason: In this chapter "sons of Benjamin" are the tribe's fighting men, so no gender setting is used. Balanced uses the tribe's name and Readable says "men"; Literal keeps the Hebrew form. The same holds for "the sons of Israel" from here to the end of the chapter: they are the gathered army of the other tribes (verses 2, 11, 17), so Balanced and Readable say "the Israelites" with no gender setting.

decisions.choice: the rest of
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that "Israel" here means the other tribes, since Benjamin is part of Israel too.

records.source: וַיַּ֜עַן הָאִ֣ישׁ הַלֵּוִ֗י אִ֛ישׁ הָאִשָּׁ֥ה הַנִּרְצָחָ֖ה וַיֹּאמַ֑ר הַגִּבְעָ֨תָה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לְבִנְיָמִ֔ן בָּ֛אתִי אֲנִ֥י וּפִֽילַגְשִׁ֖י לָלֽוּן׃
records.gloss: And answered the man the Levite, [the] husband of the woman the murdered, and said, [To] the Gibeah which [is] to Benjamin I came, I and my concubine, to spend the night.
pieces: The Levite, the husband of the murdered woman, answered, "My concubine and I came to Gibeah in Benjamin to spend the night.

L.4: And the Levite man, the husband of the woman who was murdered, answered and said, "I came to Gibeah, which belongs to Benjamin, I and my concubine, to spend the night.

R.4: The Levite whose wife had been murdered answered, "My concubine (a secondary wife) and I came to the town of Gibeah in Benjamin's land to stay for the night.

decisions.choice: the husband of the woman who was murdered: the narrator names the crime
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used for murder in the commandment (Exodus 20:13). The narrator calls her death murder before the Levite gives his account, and calls him her husband, though she was a concubine (19:1-3).

decisions.choice: concubine: a wife of lower standing
decisions.reason: A concubine was a lawful wife of lower rank than a full wife, often without a bride price or the same rights for her children. Chapter 19 calls the Levite her husband and her father his father-in-law (19:3-4).

decisions.choice: Gibeah, which belongs to Benjamin: the town of the crime
decisions.reason: The story is told in 19:12-28. Gibeah lay a few miles north of Jerusalem and was later the home of Saul, Israel's first king (1 Samuel 10:26).

decisions.choice: (a secondary wife)
decisions.reason: Readable explains "concubine" the first time it comes in the chapter.

records.source: וַיָּקֻ֤מוּ עָלַי֙ בַּעֲלֵ֣י הַגִּבְעָ֔ה וַיָּסֹ֧בּוּ עָלַ֛י אֶת־הַבַּ֖יִת לָ֑יְלָה אוֹתִי֙ דִּמּ֣וּ לַהֲרֹ֔ג וְאֶת־פִּילַגְשִׁ֥י עִנּ֖וּ וַתָּמֹֽת׃
records.gloss: And rose against me [the] lords of the Gibeah, and surrounded against me the house [by] night; me they intended to kill, and my concubine they abused, and she died.
pieces: The men of Gibeah rose against me and surrounded the house at night to get me. They meant to kill me. They raped my concubine, and she died.

L.5: And the lords of Gibeah rose against me and surrounded the house around me at night. Me they intended to kill, and my concubine they abused, and she died.

R.5: During the night the leaders of Gibeah came after me and surrounded the house where I was. They wanted to kill me. Instead they raped my concubine, and she died.

decisions.choice: the lords of Gibeah: its citizens, the men of standing in the town
decisions.reason: The word is the one used for a master or owner. Of a town it means its citizens, the free men who held its land and made its decisions (9:2). It puts the blame on the town's men, not only on a few.

decisions.choice: they intended to kill me: the Levite's own account of what they meant
decisions.reason: In 19:22 the men demanded to have sex with the man; the Levite now says they meant to kill him. He also leaves out that he himself put the woman out to them (19:25). The reader can compare his account with the story as it was told.

decisions.choice: abused: forced, raped
decisions.reason: The verb means to humble or afflict, and of a woman it means to force her (Genesis 34:2; 2 Samuel 13:14). Here it is the gang rape told in 19:25.

decisions.choice: the men of Gibeah (B); the leaders of Gibeah (R)
decisions.reason: "Lords" in English suggests nobles, so Balanced says "the men" and Readable "the leaders" (m1). Literal keeps "lords".

records.source: וָֽאֹחֵ֤ז בְּפִֽילַגְשִׁי֙ וָֽאֲנַתְּחֶ֔הָ וָֽאֲשַׁלְּחֶ֔הָ בְּכָל־שְׂדֵ֖ה נַחֲלַ֣ת יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל כִּ֥י עָשׂ֛וּ זִמָּ֥ה וּנְבָלָ֖ה בְּיִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: And I took hold of my concubine and I cut her in pieces and I sent her through all [the] field of [the] inheritance of Israel, for they have done lewdness and outrage in Israel.
pieces: So I took my concubine, cut her into pieces, and sent them throughout the whole land Israel had inherited, because they had done a shameful and outrageous thing in Israel.

L.6: And I took hold of my concubine and cut her in pieces and sent her through all the territory of the inheritance of Israel, for they have committed lewdness and an outrage in Israel.

R.6: So I took her body and cut it into pieces. I sent the pieces to every part of Israel's land, because these men had done a shameful and wicked thing in Israel.

decisions.choice: I cut her in pieces and sent her: the summons told in 19:29
decisions.reason: The same act is told in 19:29. Saul later sends pieces of oxen through Israel to call the tribes to war (1 Samuel 11:7). The pieces were a call that no tribe could ignore.

decisions.choice: lewdness and outrage: a shameful crime against what Israel must not do
decisions.reason: The first word is used for sexual wickedness that is planned (Leviticus 18:17). The second is used for acts that break the bonds of the people, such as the rape of Dinah (Genesis 34:7) and Amnon's rape of Tamar (2 Samuel 13:12). "In Israel" means such a thing is not to be done among God's people.

decisions.choice: the field of the inheritance of Israel: the whole land given to Israel
decisions.reason: "Field" here means territory, and "inheritance" is the land each tribe received as its share from God (Joshua 13-19).

decisions.choice: sent them (B); the pieces (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "sent her"; Balanced and Readable say what was sent, the pieces of her body.

records.source: הִנֵּ֥ה כֻלְּכֶ֖ם בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל הָב֥וּ לָכֶ֛ם דָּבָ֥ר וְעֵצָ֖ה הֲלֹֽם׃
records.gloss: Look, all of you [are] sons of Israel; give for yourselves word and counsel here.
pieces: Now all of you, the Israelites, give your advice and decide what to do here."

L.7: Look, all of you [are] the sons of Israel; give for yourselves word and counsel here."

R.7: All of you are the Israelites. So talk it over and decide right here what must be done."

decisions.choice: give word and counsel: decide together what to do
decisions.reason: To give a word and counsel is to speak and reach a decision. Chapter 19 ends with the same call: "consider it, take counsel, and speak" (19:30).

decisions.choice: all of you are sons of Israel: the appeal rests on their being one people
decisions.reason: The Levite appeals to them as Israel, the people the crime was done against (verse 6). Because they are all Israel, it is for all of them to decide.

decisions.choice: here
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable keep "here" to show that the decision is to be made at once, at the gathering.

records.source: וַיָּ֨קָם֙ כָּל־הָעָ֔ם כְּאִ֥ישׁ אֶחָ֖ד לֵאמֹ֑ר לֹ֤א נֵלֵךְ֙ אִ֣ישׁ לְאָהֳל֔וֹ וְלֹ֥א נָס֖וּר אִ֥ישׁ לְבֵיתֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And arose all the people as one man, saying, Not we will go, a man to his tent, and not we will turn aside, a man to his house.
pieces: All the people rose up as one and said, "None of us will go home to his tent. Not one of us will return to his house.

L.8: And all the people arose as one man, saying, "We will not go, any man to his tent, and we will not turn aside, any man to his house.

R.8: All the people stood up together and said, "Not one of us will go back home.

decisions.choice: go to his tent, turn to his house: go home
decisions.reason: "To your tents" was the call to go home (1 Kings 12:16). Here both phrases say the same thing twice, a pledge that no man would go home until the matter was dealt with.

decisions.choice: as one man
decisions.reason: As in verse 1.

decisions.choice: Not one of us will go back home
decisions.reason: Readable joins the two matching lines into one, since both say the same thing (m1).

records.source: וְעַתָּ֕ה זֶ֣ה הַדָּבָ֔ר אֲשֶׁ֥ר נַעֲשֶׂ֖ה לַגִּבְעָ֑ה עָלֶ֖יהָ בְּגוֹרָֽל׃
records.gloss: And now this [is] the thing which we will do to the Gibeah: against it by lot.
pieces: This is what we will do to Gibeah: we will go up against it as the lot decides.

L.9: And now this [is] the thing that we will do to Gibeah: [we will go up] against it by lot.

R.9: This is what we will do to Gibeah: we will cast lots to decide who goes up to attack it.

decisions.choice: against it by lot: a verb is understood, most likely "go up"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is brief and leaves out the verb. The Greek translation reads "we will go up against it by lot", which fits the next verse, where the lot picks the men who will gather supplies. It could also mean that the lot will decide which tribe attacks first, as God does in verse 18.

decisions.choice: by lot: letting God decide
decisions.reason: Casting lots was a way of leaving a choice to God (Proverbs 16:33; Joshua 7:14). The land itself had been shared out by lot (Joshua 18:10).

decisions.choice: [we will go up] / we will go up
decisions.reason: English needs the missing verb (m1). Literal brackets it.

records.source: וְלָקַ֣חְנוּ עֲשָׂרָה֩ אֲנָשִׁ֨ים לַמֵּאָ֜ה לְכֹ֣ל׀שִׁבְטֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל וּמֵאָ֤ה לָאֶ֨לֶף֙ וְאֶ֣לֶף לָרְבָבָ֔ה לָקַ֥חַת צֵדָ֖ה לָעָ֑ם לַעֲשׂ֗וֹת לְבוֹאָם֙ לְגֶ֣בַע בִּנְיָמִ֔ן כְּכָל־הַ֨נְּבָלָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשָׂ֖ה בְּיִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: And we will take ten men of [the] hundred, of all [the] tribes of Israel, and a hundred of [the] thousand, and a thousand of [the] ten thousand, to take provision for the people, to do, at their coming to Geba of Benjamin, according to all the outrage which it did in Israel.
pieces: We will take ten men out of every 100 from all the tribes of Israel, 100 out of every 1,000, and 1,000 out of every 10,000, to bring food for the army. Then, when the army comes to Gibeah in Benjamin, it can repay them for all the outrage they committed in Israel."

L.10: And we will take ten men of [every] 100 from all the tribes of Israel, and 100 of [every] 1,000, and 1,000 of [every] 10,000, to take provisions for the people, to do, when they come to Geba of Benjamin, according to all the outrage that it did in Israel."

R.10: We will choose one man in every ten from all the tribes of Israel to bring food for the army. Then the army can go to Gibeah in Benjamin and punish its people for the terrible thing they did in Israel."

decisions.choice: one in ten to bring supplies: a tenth of the army to keep the rest fed
decisions.reason: An army in the field had to be fed. One man in ten would gather food so that the rest could stay and fight until the matter was finished.

decisions.choice: Geba of Benjamin: Gibeah
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has "Geba", a short form of the same name, which elsewhere names a different town nearby (verse 33). Here it must mean Gibeah, the town of the crime, as verses 4, 5 and 9 show.

decisions.choice: to do according to all the outrage: to punish them as the deed deserves
decisions.reason: "To do according to" the outrage means to deal with them as their crime requires. The town is the one that "did" the outrage (the verb is singular).

decisions.choice: Gibeah
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "Gibeah", so the reader does not take the name for another town (m2); Literal keeps "Geba".

decisions.choice: one man in every ten
decisions.reason: Readable gives the proportion once instead of listing it three times.

records.source: וַיֵּֽאָסֵ֞ף כָּל־אִ֤ישׁ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ אֶל־הָעִ֔יר כְּאִ֥ישׁ אֶחָ֖ד חֲבֵרִֽים׃פ
records.gloss: And gathered every man of Israel to the city, as one man, joined together.
pieces: So all the men of Israel gathered against the city, united as one.

L.11: And all the men of Israel gathered against the city, as one man, joined together.

R.11: So all the men of Israel came together to fight against the town. They were completely united.

decisions.choice: to the city: against Gibeah
decisions.reason: The preposition can mean "to" or "against". The city is Gibeah, and the tribes gathered to fight it.

decisions.choice: joined together: allies bound to one purpose
decisions.reason: The word means companions or allies. It is the third time the chapter says the tribes were "as one man" (verses 1 and 8).

decisions.choice: the men of Israel
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "every man of Israel", a collective for the whole army. English says "all the men".

records.source: וַֽיִּשְׁלְח֞וּ שִׁבְטֵ֤י יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ אֲנָשִׁ֔ים בְּכָל־שִׁבְטֵ֥י בִנְיָמִ֖ן לֵאמֹ֑ר מָ֚ה הָרָעָ֣ה הַזֹּ֔את אֲשֶׁ֥ר נִהְיְתָ֖ה בָּכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And sent [the] tribes of Israel men through all [the] tribes of Benjamin, saying, What [is] the evil the this which has happened among you?
pieces: The tribes of Israel sent men through the whole tribe of Benjamin to say, "What is this evil thing that has been done among you?

L.12: And the tribes of Israel sent men through all the tribes of Benjamin, saying, "What [is] this evil that has happened among you?

R.12: The tribes of Israel sent messengers to all the clans of Benjamin. They said, "What is this evil thing that has happened among you?

decisions.choice: the tribes of Benjamin: the clans of the one tribe
decisions.reason: Benjamin was one tribe, but the Hebrew says "tribes". The plural means its family groups or clans, as the same word does in Numbers 4:18.

decisions.choice: what is this evil: a question that is also a charge
decisions.reason: The question does not ask for facts the tribes already know (verses 4-7). It calls on Benjamin to own what has been done among them.

decisions.choice: the whole tribe of Benjamin (B); all the clans of Benjamin (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced uses the singular so the reader is not misled into thinking Benjamin was several tribes; Readable says "clans" (m1). Literal keeps "tribes".

records.heading: Benjamin refuses to hand over the men of Gibeah

records.source: וְעַתָּ֡ה תְּנוּ֩ אֶת־הָאֲנָשִׁ֨ים בְּנֵֽי־בְלִיַּ֜עַל אֲשֶׁ֤ר בַּגִּבְעָה֙ וּנְמִיתֵ֔ם וּנְבַעֲרָ֥ה רָעָ֖ה מִיִּשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְלֹ֤א אָבוּ֙ בְּנֵ֣יבִּנְיָמִ֔ן לִשְׁמֹ֕עַ בְּק֖וֹל אֲחֵיהֶ֥ם בְּנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: And now give the men, [the] sons of worthlessness who [are] in the Gibeah, and we will put them to death, and we will purge [the] evil from Israel. And not were willing [the] sons of Benjamin to listen to [the] voice of their brothers, [the] sons of Israel.
pieces: Now hand over those worthless men in Gibeah, so that we can put them to death and remove this evil from Israel." But the Benjaminites would not listen to their brothers, the Israelites.

L.13: And now give [up] the men, the sons of worthlessness who [are] in Gibeah, that we may put them to death and purge the evil from Israel." But the sons of Benjamin were not willing to listen to the voice of their brothers, the sons of Israel.

R.13: Now give us those wicked men in Gibeah. We will put them to death and so remove this evil from Israel." But the men of Benjamin refused to listen to their own relatives, the rest of the Israelites.

decisions.choice: sons of worthlessness: wicked, lawless men
decisions.reason: "Sons of" a quality means men marked by it. The word means worthlessness or ruin, and it names men who break every bond of law and decency. It is the name the story gave the men of Gibeah in 19:22, and the one Deuteronomy uses for those who lead a town astray (Deuteronomy 13:14).

decisions.choice: purge the evil from Israel: the words of the law for a crime that must be punished
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy uses this phrase where a crime is so serious that the guilty must die so that the evil does not remain among the people (Deuteronomy 17:12; 22:21-22). The tribes ask first only for the guilty men, not for war.

decisions.choice: the sons of Benjamin: the reading for the margin
decisions.reason: The written Hebrew has only "Benjamin"; the traditional reading in the margin adds "the sons of". The meaning is the same either way: the tribe refused.

decisions.choice: would not listen to their brothers: Benjamin sides with the guilty men
decisions.reason: By refusing to give up the men, the tribe takes their side, and the matter becomes a war between brothers. The tribes call Benjamin "my brother" again in verses 23 and 28.

decisions.choice: worthless men (B); wicked men (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the meaning of the Hebrew expression (m1); Literal keeps "sons of worthlessness".

records.source: וַיֵּאָסְפ֧וּ בְנֵֽי־בִנְיָמִ֛ן מִן־הֶעָרִ֖ים הַגִּבְעָ֑תָה לָצֵ֥את לַמִּלְחָמָ֖ה עִם־בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: And gathered [the] sons of Benjamin from the cities to the Gibeah, to go out to the battle with [the] sons of Israel.
pieces: Instead the Benjaminites came together from their towns to Gibeah, to go out and fight against the Israelites.

L.14: And the sons of Benjamin gathered from the cities to Gibeah, to go out to battle against the sons of Israel.

R.14: Instead the men of Benjamin left their towns and gathered at Gibeah to fight against the Israelites.

decisions.choice: they gathered from the cities to Gibeah: the whole tribe came to defend the guilty town
decisions.reason: Benjamin's answer is not to give up the guilty men but to bring its army to Gibeah. The verb is the same one used of Israel gathering in verse 11: two armies now gather against each other.

decisions.choice: to go out to battle (L); to go out and fight (B); to fight (R)
decisions.reason: "Going out to battle" is the chapter's phrase for marching out to fight (verses 20, 23, 28). Literal keeps it each time; Balanced and Readable say "fight".

records.source: וַיִּתְפָּֽקְדוּ֩ בְנֵ֨י בִנְיָמִ֜ן בַּיּ֤וֹם הַהוּא֙ מֵהֶ֣עָרִ֔ים עֶשְׂרִ֨ים וְשִׁשָּׁ֥ה אֶ֛לֶף אִ֖ישׁ שֹׁ֣לֵֽף חָ֑רֶב לְ֠בַד מִיֹּשְׁבֵ֤י הַגִּבְעָה֙ הִתְפָּ֣קְד֔וּ שְׁבַ֥ע מֵא֖וֹת אִ֥ישׁ בָּחֽוּר׃
records.gloss: And mustered themselves [the] sons of Benjamin on the day the that from the cities: twenty and six thousand man drawing [the] sword, apart from [the] inhabitants of the Gibeah, [who] mustered themselves: seven hundred man chosen.
pieces: That day the Benjaminites called up from their towns 26,000 men armed with swords, besides the people of Gibeah, who called up 700 chosen men.

L.15: And the sons of Benjamin mustered themselves on that day from the cities: 26,000 men drawing [the] sword, apart from the inhabitants of Gibeah, who mustered themselves, 700 chosen men.

R.15: That day Benjamin's towns counted 26,000 soldiers armed with swords. Gibeah itself added 700 of its best men.

decisions.choice: mustered themselves: were counted for war
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used for counting men in a census (Numbers 1:3). Here it is a count of those who would fight.

decisions.choice: 26,000: the number in the Hebrew text
decisions.reason: Some copies of the Greek translation have a smaller number, 25,000 or 23,000. The Hebrew number fits the totals later in the chapter: 25,100 Benjaminites fall (verse 35) and 600 escape (verse 47), close to 26,000 plus the 700 men of Gibeah. On the size of such numbers see verse 2.

decisions.choice: chosen men: picked, trained fighters
decisions.reason: The word means men who were selected, the best fighters. Verse 16 describes them further.

decisions.choice: called up (B); counted (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable avoid the formal word "mustered"; Literal keeps it.

records.source: מִכֹּ֣ל׀הָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֗ה שְׁבַ֤ע מֵאוֹת֙ אִ֣ישׁ בָּח֔וּר אִטֵּ֖ר יַד־יְמִינ֑וֹ כָּל־זֶ֗ה קֹלֵ֧עַ בָּאֶ֛בֶן אֶל־הַֽשַּׂעֲרָ֖ה וְלֹ֥א יַחֲטִֽא׃פ
records.gloss: From all the people the this [were] seven hundred man chosen, restricted [in the] hand of his right; every this [one] slinging with the stone at the hair, and not missing.
pieces: Among all these soldiers were 700 picked men who fought left-handed, each able to sling a stone at a hair without missing.

L.16: Of all this people [there were] 700 chosen men restricted [in] their right hand; every one of these could sling with a stone at a hair and not miss.

R.16: Among these soldiers were 700 of the best fighters who were left-handed. Each of them could throw a stone with a sling and hit something as thin as a hair without missing.

decisions.choice: restricted in his right hand: left-handed
decisions.reason: As at 3:15, where the same words describe Ehud of Benjamin. These men fought with the left hand, which made them harder to defend against. 1 Chronicles 12:2 tells of Benjaminites who could sling stones with either hand. The irony is the same as at 3:15: Benjamin means "son of the right hand".

decisions.choice: 700 chosen men: most likely the 700 of Gibeah from verse 15
decisions.reason: The same number and the same words, "700 chosen men", come in both verses, so the left-handed slingers are most likely Gibeah's 700. The verse could also describe a further group chosen from the whole Benjaminite army.

decisions.choice: slinging with a stone: a deadly weapon in skilled hands
decisions.reason: A sling was a pouch on two cords, swung to hurl a stone with great force. Slingers could strike from beyond the reach of swords, as David did (1 Samuel 17:49).

decisions.choice: not miss: the verb also means "sin"
decisions.reason: The verb means to miss a target or a goal. It is the usual word for sinning, falling short of what God requires, but here it has its plain sense.

decisions.choice: something as thin as a hair
decisions.reason: Readable says what hitting "a hair" means: a target so small it could hardly be seen.

records.source: וְאִ֨ישׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל הִתְפָּֽקְד֗וּ לְבַד֙ מִבִּנְיָמִ֔ן אַרְבַּ֨ע מֵא֥וֹת אֶ֛לֶף אִ֖ישׁ שֹׁ֣לֵֽף חָ֑רֶב כָּל־זֶ֖ה אִ֥ישׁ מִלְחָמָֽה׃
records.gloss: And [the] men of Israel mustered themselves, apart from Benjamin: four hundred thousand man drawing [the] sword; every this [one was a] man of war.
pieces: The men of Israel, not counting Benjamin, called up 400,000 men armed with swords, all of them experienced fighters.

L.17: And the men of Israel mustered themselves, apart from Benjamin, 400,000 men drawing [the] sword; every one of these [was] a man of war.

R.17: Israel, not counting Benjamin, had 400,000 soldiers armed with swords. All of them were trained for war.

decisions.choice: 400,000: the same number as verse 2
decisions.reason: The count agrees with the gathering at Mizpah (verse 2). On the size of the number see the note there. Against 26,700 Benjaminites, the tribes' army was about fifteen times larger.

decisions.choice: a man of war: a soldier, a fighting man
decisions.reason: The phrase names a trained, seasoned warrior (Joshua 17:1; 1 Samuel 16:18).

decisions.choice: the men of Israel
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "the man of Israel", a collective for the army. Here and through the chapter English says "the men of Israel".

records.source: וַיָּקֻ֜מוּ וַיַּעֲל֣וּ בֵֽית־אֵל֮ וַיִּשְׁאֲל֣וּ בֵאלֹהִים֒ וַיֹּֽאמְרוּ֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל מִ֚י יַעֲלֶה־לָּ֣נוּ בַתְּחִלָּ֔ה לַמִּלְחָמָ֖ה עִם־בְּנֵ֣י בִנְיָמִ֑ן וַיֹּ֥אמֶר יְהוָ֖ה יְהוּדָ֥ה בַתְּחִלָּֽה׃
records.gloss: And they arose and went up [to] Bethel and asked of God, and said [the] sons of Israel, Who will go up for us at the first to the battle with [the] sons of Benjamin? And said Yahweh, Judah at the first.
pieces: The Israelites set out and went up to Bethel, and they asked God, "Which of us should go up first to fight against the Benjaminites?" {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} answered, "Judah is to go first."

L.18: And they arose and went up to Bethel and asked God, and the sons of Israel said, "Who will go up for us first to the battle against the sons of Benjamin?" And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said, "Judah first."

R.18: The Israelites went up to Bethel and asked God for guidance. "Which tribe should go first to attack the men of Benjamin?" they asked. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} answered, "Judah will go first."

decisions.choice: asked God: sought God's answer through the priest
decisions.reason: To ask of God is to seek his decision, which in Israel was given through the priest (Numbers 27:21). Verses 27-28 say that the ark was at Bethel and Phinehas the priest served before it. The tribes ask in this way three times in this chapter (verses 18, 23, 27).

decisions.choice: Bethel: the town, not "the house of God"
decisions.reason: The name means "house of God" and is written as two words here. It is the town of that name, north of Gibeah, where the ark was at this time (verse 27). It is the place where God met Jacob (Genesis 28:19).

decisions.choice: who will go up first ... Judah first: the question that opens the book
decisions.reason: The tribes ask the same question in 1:1, and receive the same answer, "Judah" (1:2). There the enemy was the Canaanites; here it is Benjamin, one of Israel's own tribes. Unlike 1:2, God gives no promise of victory here.

decisions.choice: asked God (L, B); asked God for guidance (R)
decisions.reason: The same wording is used every time the tribes ask God or the LORD (verses 23, 27), as at 1:1. Readable says what the asking was for (m1).

decisions.choice: Which tribe; will go
decisions.reason: The answer names a tribe, so Readable says "tribe" in the question, as at 1:1.

records.source: וַיָּק֥וּמוּ בְנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בַּבֹּ֑קֶר וַיַּֽחֲנ֖וּ עַל־הַגִּבְעָֽה׃פ
records.gloss: And arose [the] sons of Israel in the morning and they camped against the Gibeah.
pieces: The next morning the Israelites set out and camped facing Gibeah.

L.19: And the sons of Israel arose in the morning and camped against Gibeah.

R.19: The next morning the Israelites marched out and set up camp near Gibeah.

decisions.choice: camped against Gibeah: took up a position to attack the town
decisions.reason: To camp "against" a town is to set up camp facing it, ready to attack (Joshua 10:5).

decisions.choice: set out (B); marched out (R)
decisions.reason: "Arose" here means getting up and starting out, not only rising from sleep.

records.source: וַיֵּצֵא֙ אִ֣ישׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל לַמִּלְחָמָ֖ה עִם־בִּנְיָמִ֑ן וַיַּעַרְכ֨וּ אִתָּ֧ם אִֽישׁ־יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל מִלְחָמָ֖ה אֶל־הַגִּבְעָֽה׃
records.gloss: And went out [the] men of Israel to the battle with Benjamin, and arranged with them [the] men of Israel battle at the Gibeah.
pieces: The men of Israel went out to fight Benjamin and drew up their battle lines against them at Gibeah.

L.20: And the men of Israel went out to battle against Benjamin, and the men of Israel arranged [the] battle [line] against them at Gibeah.

R.20: The men of Israel went out to fight against Benjamin. They took their positions for battle at Gibeah.

decisions.choice: arranged battle: drew up the army in its lines
decisions.reason: The verb means to set things in order. With "battle" it means placing the army in its ranks, ready to fight (1 Samuel 17:2, 8). The same phrase comes in verses 22, 30 and 33.

decisions.choice: arranged [the] battle [line] (L); drew up their battle lines (B); took their positions for battle (R)
decisions.reason: The same wording is used for this phrase at each level through the chapter (verses 22, 30, 33).

records.heading: War against Benjamin

records.source: וַיֵּצְא֥וּ בְנֵֽי־בִנְיָמִ֖ן מִן־הַגִּבְעָ֑ה וַיַּשְׁחִ֨יתוּ בְיִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא שְׁנַ֨יִם וְעֶשְׂרִ֥ים אֶ֛לֶף אִ֖ישׁ אָֽרְצָה׃
records.gloss: And went out [the] sons of Benjamin from the Gibeah, and they destroyed in Israel on the day the that two and twenty thousand man to [the] ground.
pieces: Then the Benjaminites came out of Gibeah and cut down 22,000 men of Israel on the battlefield that day.

L.21: And the sons of Benjamin came out from Gibeah, and they destroyed in Israel on that day 22,000 men to the ground.

R.21: Then the men of Benjamin came out of Gibeah and attacked. That day they killed 22,000 Israelite soldiers.

decisions.choice: destroyed ... to the ground: struck them down dead on the field
decisions.reason: The verb means to ruin or destroy. "To the ground" pictures the men falling where they fought. The phrase comes again in verse 25.

decisions.choice: 22,000: the tribes lose though God sent them
decisions.reason: The tribes asked God and went up as he said (verse 18), yet they are beaten. Though God told them who should go first, he did not promise them victory. The defeat sends them back to weep before the LORD (verse 23). On the size of the number see verse 2.

decisions.choice: destroyed ... to the ground (L); cut down ... on the battlefield (B); killed (R)
decisions.reason: The same wording is used again in verse 25.

records.source: וַיִּתְחַזֵּ֥ק הָעָ֖ם אִ֣ישׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיֹּסִ֨פוּ֙ לַעֲרֹ֣ךְ מִלְחָמָ֔ה בַּמָּק֕וֹם אֲשֶׁר־עָ֥רְכוּ שָׁ֖ם בַּיּ֥וֹם הָרִאשֽׁוֹן׃
records.gloss: And strengthened itself the people, [the] men of Israel, and they again arranged battle in the place where they had arranged there on the day the first.
pieces: But the army, the men of Israel, took courage and again drew up their battle lines in the same place where they had drawn them up on the first day.

L.22: And the people, the men of Israel, strengthened themselves, and they again arranged [the] battle [line] in the place where they had arranged [it] on the first day.

R.22: But the Israelite army did not give up. They took courage and took their positions for battle again in the same place as on the first day.

decisions.choice: they again arranged battle: a summary told before the account of how it came about
decisions.reason: Verse 23, which comes next, tells of the weeping and the asking of the LORD that led to this second battle. Hebrew stories often give the outcome first and then go back to tell how it came about.

decisions.choice: strengthened itself: took courage, gathered its strength
decisions.reason: The verb means to make oneself strong. After losing 22,000 men, the army did not scatter but took heart to fight again.

decisions.choice: the people: the army
decisions.reason: "The people" in a story of war often means the fighting men, as here, where it is explained as "the men of Israel".

decisions.choice: arranged [the] battle [line] / drew up their battle lines / took their positions for battle
decisions.reason: As in verse 20.

records.source: וַיַּעֲל֣וּ בְנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל וַיִּבְכּ֣וּ לִפְנֵֽי־יְהוָה֮ עַד־הָעֶרֶב֒ וַיִּשְׁאֲל֤וּ בַֽיהוָה֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר הַאוֹסִ֗יף לָגֶ֨שֶׁת֙ לַמִּלְחָמָ֔ה עִם־בְּנֵ֥י בִנְיָמִ֖ן אָחִ֑י וַיֹּ֥אמֶר יְהוָ֖ה עֲל֥וּ אֵלָֽיו׃פ
records.gloss: And went up [the] sons of Israel and wept before Yahweh until the evening, and asked of Yahweh, saying, Shall I again draw near to the battle with [the] sons of Benjamin my brother? And said Yahweh, Go up against him.
pieces: The Israelites went up and wept before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} until evening, and they asked {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, "Should we again go into battle against our brothers the Benjaminites?" {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} answered, "Go up against them."

L.23: And the sons of Israel went up and wept before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} until the evening, and they asked {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, saying, "Shall I again draw near to battle against the sons of Benjamin my brother?" And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said, "Go up against him."

R.23: The Israelites went up and cried before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} until evening. They asked {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} for guidance. "Should we fight against the men of Benjamin again? They are our relatives," they said. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} answered, "Go and attack them."

decisions.choice: they went up and wept: what happened before the battle of verse 22
decisions.reason: This verse goes back to tell what the tribes did between the two battles, as noted at verse 22. "Went up" is most likely to Bethel, where they asked God in verse 18 and go again in verse 26.

decisions.choice: shall I ... my brother: Israel speaks as one person of Benjamin as its brother
decisions.reason: The Hebrew uses "I" and "my", as if Israel were a single man asking whether to fight his brother. The question now is not who should lead but whether to fight at all.

decisions.choice: asked the LORD
decisions.reason: As in verse 18: the tribes sought God's decision through the priest.

decisions.choice: go up against him: permission, but still no promise
decisions.reason: God tells them to go, but as in verse 18 he does not say they will win. Only at the third asking, after fasting and offerings, does he promise victory (verse 28).

decisions.choice: asked (L, B); asked ... for guidance (R)
decisions.reason: As in verse 18.

decisions.choice: we ... our brothers ... them
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the plural, since the whole people is speaking of a whole tribe; Literal keeps the singular (m2).

records.source: וַיִּקְרְב֧וּ בְנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל אֶל־בְּנֵ֥י בִנְיָמִ֖ן בַּיּ֥וֹם הַשֵּׁנִֽי׃
records.gloss: And drew near [the] sons of Israel to [the] sons of Benjamin on the day the second.
pieces: So the Israelites advanced against the Benjaminites on the second day.

L.24: And the sons of Israel drew near to the sons of Benjamin on the second day.

R.24: So on the second day the Israelites went out against the men of Benjamin.

decisions.choice: drew near: advanced to fight
decisions.reason: The verb is the one in the question of verse 23, "Shall I again draw near to battle?" The tribes do what they asked about.

decisions.choice: advanced
decisions.reason: In a battle "drew near" means moved forward to attack, so Balanced says "advanced".

records.source: וַיֵּצֵא֩ בִנְיָמִ֨ן׀לִקְרָאתָ֥ם׀מִֽן־הַגִּבְעָה֮ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַשֵּׁנִי֒ וַיַּשְׁחִיתוּ֩ בִבְנֵ֨י יִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל ע֗וֹד שְׁמֹנַ֨ת עָשָׂ֥ר אֶ֛לֶף אִ֖ישׁ אָ֑רְצָה כָּל־אֵ֖לֶּה שֹׁ֥לְפֵי חָֽרֶב׃
records.gloss: And went out Benjamin to meet them from the Gibeah on the day the second, and they destroyed among [the] sons of Israel again eighteen thousand man to [the] ground; all these [were] drawing [the] sword.
pieces: Benjamin came out of Gibeah to meet them on the second day and again cut down 18,000 of the Israelites on the battlefield, all of them armed with swords.

L.25: And Benjamin went out to meet them from Gibeah on the second day, and they destroyed among the sons of Israel again 18,000 men to the ground; all these [were] drawing [the] sword.

R.25: On the second day Benjamin's army came out of Gibeah to meet them. Again they killed many Israelites: 18,000 soldiers, all armed with swords.

decisions.choice: again 18,000: a second defeat after God said "go up"
decisions.reason: The tribes went up because the LORD told them to (verse 23), and they lose again. In two days they have lost 40,000 men. The story does not explain why; it shows the tribes driven to seek God more deeply in verse 26. On the size of the number see verse 2.

decisions.choice: destroyed ... to the ground
decisions.reason: As in verse 21.

decisions.choice: destroyed ... to the ground (L); cut down ... on the battlefield (B); killed (R)
decisions.reason: As in verse 21.

records.source: וַיַּעֲל֣וּ כָל־בְּנֵי֩ יִשְׂרָאֵ֨ל וְכָל־הָעָ֜ם וַיָּבֹ֣אוּ בֵֽית־אֵ֗ל וַיִּבְכּוּ֙ וַיֵּ֤שְׁבוּ שָׁם֙ לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה וַיָּצ֥וּמוּ בַיּוֹם־הַה֖וּא עַד־הָעָ֑רֶב וַֽיַּעֲל֛וּ עֹל֥וֹת וּשְׁלָמִ֖ים לִפְנֵ֥י יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: And went up all [the] sons of Israel and all the people and came [to] Bethel, and wept and sat there before Yahweh, and fasted on the day the that until the evening, and offered up burnt offerings and peace offerings before Yahweh.
pieces: Then all the Israelites, the whole army, went up to Bethel. They sat there weeping before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and they fasted that day until evening and offered burnt offerings and peace offerings before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.26: And all the sons of Israel and all the people went up and came to Bethel, and they wept and sat there before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and they fasted on that day until the evening, and offered burnt offerings and peace offerings before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.26: Then all the Israelites, the whole army, went up to Bethel. They sat there and cried before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. They went without food all that day until evening. They offered burnt offerings and peace offerings to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: all the sons of Israel and all the people: the whole army together
decisions.reason: "The people" most likely means the fighting men, as in verse 22, so the two phrases say together that every one of them came. It could also mean that others besides the soldiers came with them.

decisions.choice: wept, sat, fasted: mourning and humbling themselves before God
decisions.reason: Sitting, weeping and fasting until evening were signs of grief and of seeking God with the whole heart (2 Samuel 12:16; Joel 2:12). Compared with verse 23, the tribes now add fasting and offerings: they come to God more humbly than before.

decisions.choice: burnt offerings and peace offerings
decisions.reason: The burnt offering was wholly burned on the altar for God (Leviticus 1). The peace offering was shared, part burned and part eaten by the worshipers (Leviticus 3). Together they sought God's favor and fellowship with him.

decisions.choice: the whole army
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable take "all the people" as explaining "all the Israelites" (m1). Literal keeps the two phrases side by side.

decisions.choice: went without food
decisions.reason: Readable says what fasting is.

records.source: וַיִּשְׁאֲל֥וּ בְנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בַּֽיהוָ֑ה וְשָׁ֗ם אֲרוֹן֙ בְּרִ֣ית הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים בַּיָּמִ֖ים הָהֵֽם׃
records.gloss: And asked [the] sons of Israel of Yahweh, and there [was the] ark of [the] covenant of the God in the days the those,
pieces: And the Israelites asked {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. The ark of the covenant of God was kept there in those days,

L.27: And the sons of Israel asked {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} (and there [was] the ark of the covenant of God in those days,

R.27: Then the Israelites asked {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} for guidance. At that time the ark of God's covenant was there in Bethel.

decisions.choice: the ark of the covenant of God: the sign of God's presence with Israel
decisions.reason: The ark was the chest that held the covenant tablets (Exodus 25:10-22; Deuteronomy 10:1-5). Where it was kept, there the priests sought God's answers for the people. This is the only time the book of Judges mentions it.

decisions.choice: there in those days: a note added to explain where and how they asked
decisions.reason: The narrator breaks off between "they asked" and the question (verse 28) to say that the ark was at Bethel at that time and who served before it. It explains why the tribes went to Bethel. Later the ark was kept at Shiloh (1 Samuel 4:3-4).

decisions.choice: asked the LORD
decisions.reason: As in verse 18.

decisions.choice: asked (L, B); asked ... for guidance (R)
decisions.reason: As in verse 18.

decisions.choice: in Bethel
decisions.reason: Readable says where "there" was (verse 26).

records.source: וּ֠פִינְחָס בֶּן־אֶלְעָזָ֨ר בֶּֽן־אַהֲרֹ֜ן עֹמֵ֣ד׀לְפָנָ֗יו בַּיָּמִ֣ים הָהֵם֮ לֵאמֹר֒ הַאוֹסִ֨ף ע֜וֹד לָצֵ֧את לַמִּלְחָמָ֛ה עִם־בְּנֵֽי־בִנְיָמִ֥ן אָחִ֖י אִם־אֶחְדָּ֑ל וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ עֲל֔וּ כִּ֥י מָחָ֖ר אֶתְּנֶ֥נּוּ בְיָדֶֽךָ׃
records.gloss: and Phinehas, son of Eleazar, son of Aaron, standing before it in the days the those), saying, Shall I again yet go out to the battle with [the] sons of Benjamin my brother, or shall I cease? And said Yahweh, Go up, for tomorrow I will give him into your hand.
pieces: and Phinehas son of Eleazar, son of Aaron, served before it. They asked, "Should we go out again to fight against our brothers the Benjaminites, or should we stop?" {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} answered, "Go up, for tomorrow I will hand them over to you."

L.28: and Phinehas son of Eleazar, son of Aaron, was standing before it in those days), saying, "Shall I yet again go out to battle against the sons of Benjamin my brother, or shall I stop?" And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said, "Go up, for tomorrow I will give him into your hand."

R.28: Phinehas, the grandson of Aaron, was the priest who served there. The Israelites asked, "Should we go out and fight against our relatives, the men of Benjamin, again? Or should we stop?" {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} answered, "Go and attack them. Tomorrow I will give you victory over them."

decisions.choice: Phinehas son of Eleazar, son of Aaron: the priest of the generation after Moses
decisions.reason: Phinehas is the grandson of Aaron who stood against Israel's sin at Peor (Numbers 25:7-13) and served in Joshua's time (Joshua 22:13). His name shows that these events took place early in the time of the judges, though the book tells them near its end.

decisions.choice: standing before it: serving as priest before the ark
decisions.reason: To "stand before" the LORD or his ark is to serve him as a priest (Deuteronomy 10:8; 18:7).

decisions.choice: tomorrow I will give him into your hand: now God promises victory
decisions.reason: For the first time in the chapter the LORD's answer includes a promise. The tribes asked twice before and lost; now, after fasting and offerings, they ask whether to stop, and God says he will give them the victory.

decisions.choice: or shall I cease: the tribes are ready to give up
decisions.reason: The question now has two sides. After two defeats the tribes ask whether they should stop fighting their brother altogether.

decisions.choice: we ... our brothers ... them ... you
decisions.reason: As in verse 23, Balanced and Readable use the plural for Israel and Benjamin. Readable also says "give you victory" for "give him into your hand" (1:2).

decisions.choice: the grandson of Aaron, was the priest who served there
decisions.reason: Readable says how Phinehas was related to Aaron and what his standing before the ark meant (m1, m2), and starts a new sentence for the question.

records.source: וַיָּ֤שֶׂם יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ אֹֽרְבִ֔ים אֶל־הַגִּבְעָ֖ה סָבִֽיב׃פ
records.gloss: And set Israel ambushers against the Gibeah around.
pieces: So Israel set men in ambush all around Gibeah.

L.29: And Israel set ambushers around Gibeah.

R.29: So Israel hid soldiers all around Gibeah, ready to make a surprise attack.

decisions.choice: ambushers: the plan that took Ai
decisions.reason: The tribes use the plan Joshua used against Ai: one force draws the defenders out of the city, while a hidden force waits to enter it behind them (Joshua 8:2-22). The rest of the chapter follows the same steps.

decisions.choice: around Gibeah: on more than one side of the town
decisions.reason: "Around" suggests men hidden at several points. Verse 33 tells of the main ambush coming from the west of Geba.

decisions.choice: hid soldiers ... ready to make a surprise attack
decisions.reason: Readable says what an ambush is.

records.source: וַיַּעֲל֧וּ בְנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל אֶל־בְּנֵ֥י בִנְיָמִ֖ן בַּיּ֣וֹם הַשְּׁלִישִׁ֑י וַיַּעַרְכ֥וּ אֶל־הַגִּבְעָ֖ה כְּפַ֥עַם בְּפָֽעַם׃
records.gloss: And went up [the] sons of Israel against [the] sons of Benjamin on the day the third, and arranged against the Gibeah as time by time.
pieces: On the third day the Israelites went up against the Benjaminites and drew up their battle lines against Gibeah as they had done before.

L.30: And the sons of Israel went up against the sons of Benjamin on the third day, and arranged [the] battle [line] against Gibeah as time by time.

R.30: On the third day the Israelites went up to fight the men of Benjamin. They took their positions for battle at Gibeah just as they had done the other times.

decisions.choice: as time by time: as on the other occasions
decisions.reason: The phrase means "as before", the same way they had done twice already. It is part of the plan: Benjamin is to think this is one more battle like the others (verse 32).

decisions.choice: arranged
decisions.reason: As in verse 20: drew up the army for battle; here the word "battle" is understood.

decisions.choice: arranged [the] battle [line] / drew up their battle lines / took their positions for battle
decisions.reason: As in verse 20. Literal brackets "the battle line", which the Hebrew leaves understood here.

records.source: וַיֵּצְא֤וּ בְנֵֽי־בִנְיָמִן֙ לִקְרַ֣את הָעָ֔ם הָנְתְּק֖וּ מִן־הָעִ֑יר וַיָּחֵ֡לּוּ לְהַכּוֹת֩ מֵהָעָ֨ם חֲלָלִ֜ים כְּפַ֣עַם׀בְּפַ֗עַם בַּֽמְסִלּוֹת֙ אֲשֶׁ֨ר אַחַ֜ת עֹלָ֣ה בֵֽית־אֵ֗ל וְאַחַ֤ת גִּבְעָ֨תָה֙ בַּשָּׂדֶ֔ה כִּשְׁלֹשִׁ֥ים אִ֖ישׁ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: And went out [the] sons of Benjamin to meet the people; they were drawn away from the city. And they began to strike from the people slain, as time by time, on the highways, of which one goes up [to] Bethel and one to Gibeah in the field, about thirty man in Israel.
pieces: The Benjaminites came out to meet the army and were drawn away from the town. As before, they began to strike down some of the troops on the roads, one leading up to Bethel and the other to Gibeah, in the open country. They killed about thirty men of Israel.

L.31: And the sons of Benjamin went out to meet the people; they were drawn away from the city. And they began to strike [some] of the people, slain as time by time, on the highways, one of which goes up to Bethel and one to Gibeah in the field, about thirty men in Israel.

R.31: The men of Benjamin came out to fight the army, and the Israelites led them away from the town. As before, the men of Benjamin began killing some of the soldiers in the open country along the roads. One road went to Bethel and the other to Gibeah. They killed about thirty men of Israel.

decisions.choice: they were drawn away from the city: pulled away by the tribes' pretended retreat
decisions.reason: The verb is passive: the Benjaminites were led away from Gibeah without knowing it. Verse 32 tells how the tribes planned it, and Joshua 8:16 uses the same verb of the men of Ai.

decisions.choice: Gibeah in the field: as the Hebrew has it, though Gibeah is the city they left
decisions.reason: The Benjaminites have just left Gibeah, so a road "to Gibeah" is surprising. It may mean a road back toward Gibeah across open country. It may also be a slip for Gibeon, a town to the west whose name is very like it in Hebrew; the Hebrew text has Gibeah.

decisions.choice: highways: the main roads
decisions.reason: The word means a built-up road or highway. Fighting on the roads in open country, away from the town, was what the tribes wanted (verse 32).

decisions.choice: They killed about thirty men of Israel.
decisions.reason: Balanced puts the number in its own sentence; in the Hebrew it comes at the end of the long description of the roads.

decisions.choice: the Israelites led them
decisions.reason: Readable makes the passive verb active and says who drew them away (m1).

records.source: וַיֹּֽאמְרוּ֙ בְּנֵ֣י בִנְיָמִ֔ן נִגָּפִ֥ים הֵ֛ם לְפָנֵ֖ינוּ כְּבָרִאשֹׁנָ֑ה וּבְנֵ֧י יִשְׂרָאֵ֣ל אָמְר֗וּ נָנ֨וּסָה֙ וּֽנְתַקְּנֻ֔הוּ מִן־הָעִ֖יר אֶל־הַֽמְסִלּֽוֹת׃
records.gloss: And said [the] sons of Benjamin, They are struck down before us as at the first. And [the] sons of Israel said, Let us flee and draw him away from the city to the highways.
pieces: The Benjaminites said, "They are being beaten by us as they were before." But the Israelites had said, "Let us run away and draw them out from the town onto the roads."

L.32: And the sons of Benjamin said, "They are struck down before us as at the first." But the sons of Israel said, "Let us flee and draw him away from the city to the highways."

R.32: The men of Benjamin said, "We are beating them, just as we did before." But the Israelites had planned this. They had said, "Let us run away, so that we can lead them away from the town and onto the roads."

decisions.choice: and the sons of Israel said: the plan made before the battle
decisions.reason: The Hebrew joins the two sayings side by side. The tribes' words are the plan they had made beforehand, now told to show why Benjamin was wrong.

decisions.choice: struck down: defeated
decisions.reason: The verb is used of an army beaten in battle (verse 36; 1 Samuel 4:2).

decisions.choice: had said (B); had planned this. They had said (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable show that the tribes' words came before, as the plan (m1).

records.source: וְכֹ֣ל׀אִ֣ישׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל קָ֚מוּ מִמְּקוֹמ֔וֹ וַיַּעַרְכ֖וּ בְּבַ֣עַל תָּמָ֑ר וְאֹרֵ֧ב יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל מֵגִ֥יחַ מִמְּקֹמ֖וֹ מִמַּֽעֲרֵה־גָֽבַע׃
records.gloss: And every man of Israel rose from his place and arranged at Baal-tamar, and [the] ambush of Israel [was] bursting out from its place, from [the] open place of Geba.
pieces: All the men of Israel rose up from where they were and drew up their battle lines at Baal-tamar, while the men of Israel in ambush burst out from their position west of Geba.

L.33: And all the men of Israel rose from their place and arranged [the battle line] at Baal-tamar, and the ambush of Israel was bursting out from its place, from the open place of Geba.

R.33: The main Israelite army left its position and took its positions for battle at Baal-tamar. At the same time the soldiers who were hiding west of Geba rushed out from their hiding place.

decisions.choice: Baal-tamar: a place near Gibeah, not known today
decisions.reason: The name means "lord of the palm tree". Its site is not known, but it lay near Gibeah, where the main army turned to fight.

decisions.choice: the open place of Geba: a clearing near Geba, or west of Geba
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word is rare and may mean a bare or open place. The Greek translation and the Latin read it as "west of" and some read "Gibeah" for "Geba". The ambush came out from an open area beside one of these two towns.

decisions.choice: was bursting out: at the same moment
decisions.reason: The verb form describes action going on at the same time as the main army's turn. As the army turned to face Benjamin, the ambush rushed out behind them.

decisions.choice: west of Geba
decisions.reason: Balanced follows the reading "west of" as the most likely sense of the rare word (m2); Literal keeps "the open place". Readable also says "west".

decisions.choice: arranged [the battle line] / drew up their battle lines / took its positions for battle
decisions.reason: As in verse 20.

records.source: וַיָּבֹאוּ֩ מִנֶּ֨גֶד לַגִּבְעָ֜ה עֲשֶׂרֶת֩ אֲלָפִ֨ים אִ֤ישׁ בָּחוּר֙ מִכָּל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְהַמִּלְחָמָ֖ה כָּבֵ֑דָה וְהֵם֙ לֹ֣א יָדְע֔וּ כִּֽי־נֹגַ֥עַת עֲלֵיהֶ֖ם הָרָעָֽה׃פ
records.gloss: And came from before the Gibeah ten thousand man chosen from all Israel, and the battle [was] heavy; and they did not know that touching upon them [was] the disaster.
pieces: Then 10,000 chosen men from all Israel came against Gibeah, and the fighting was fierce. The Benjaminites did not realize that disaster was about to strike them.

L.34: And there came from opposite Gibeah 10,000 chosen men from all Israel, and the battle was heavy; and they did not know that the disaster was touching them.

R.34: Then 10,000 of Israel's best soldiers attacked Gibeah. The fighting was hard. The men of Benjamin did not know that disaster was about to fall on them.

decisions.choice: came from before Gibeah: came at Gibeah from the front, or from opposite it
decisions.reason: The words "from before" may mean the ambush came from the side facing Gibeah, or that the 10,000 attacked the town head on. Either way it is the force that would take Gibeah.

decisions.choice: they did not know: the Benjaminites
decisions.reason: "They" are the men of Benjamin, still fighting on the roads, who did not see the ambush taking their town behind them (verses 40-41).

decisions.choice: the disaster touching them: ruin about to reach them
decisions.reason: The word is the same one used for the "evil" of Gibeah in verses 3, 12 and 13. The evil that Benjamin refused to remove now comes upon them as disaster.

decisions.choice: The Benjaminites / The men of Benjamin
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say who "they" are (m2).

records.source: וַיִּגֹּ֨ף יְהוָ֥ה׀אֶֽת־בִּנְיָמִן֮ לִפְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵל֒ וַיַּשְׁחִיתוּ֩ בְנֵ֨י יִשְׂרָאֵ֤ל בְּבִנְיָמִן֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא עֶשְׂרִ֨ים וַחֲמִשָּׁ֥ה אֶ֛לֶף וּמֵאָ֖ה אִ֑ישׁ כָּל־אֵ֖לֶּה שֹׁ֥לֵף חָֽרֶב׃
records.gloss: And struck Yahweh Benjamin before Israel, and destroyed [the] sons of Israel in Benjamin on the day the that twenty and five thousand and a hundred man; all these [were] drawing [the] sword.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} defeated Benjamin before Israel, and that day the Israelites cut down 25,100 men of Benjamin, all of them armed with swords.

L.35: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} struck Benjamin before Israel, and the sons of Israel destroyed in Benjamin on that day 25,100 men; all these [were] drawing [the] sword.

R.35: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} gave Israel victory over Benjamin. That day the Israelites killed 25,100 of Benjamin's soldiers, all armed with swords.

decisions.choice: the LORD struck Benjamin: the victory is God's
decisions.reason: The verb is the one Benjamin used of Israel in verse 32. Now it is the LORD who strikes, as he promised in verse 28. The battle is told as his act first, and only then as Israel's.

decisions.choice: 25,100: a summary of the whole battle, told before the details
decisions.reason: This verse gives the result of the day. Verses 36-46 go back and tell how the battle went, step by step, ending with a round total of 25,000 (verse 46). On the size of the numbers see verse 2.

decisions.choice: defeated Benjamin before Israel (B); gave Israel victory over Benjamin (R)
decisions.reason: "Struck before" means defeated in front of, or for, Israel. Readable says plainly that God gave the victory.

records.heading: Benjamin is defeated

records.source: וַיִּרְא֥וּ בְנֵֽי־בִנְיָמִ֖ן כִּ֣י נִגָּ֑פוּ וַיִּתְּנ֨וּ אִֽישׁ־יִשְׂרָאֵ֤ל מָקוֹם֙ לְבִנְיָמִ֔ן כִּ֤י בָֽטְחוּ֙ אֶל־הָ֣אֹרֵ֔ב אֲשֶׁר שָׂ֖מוּ אֶל־הַגִּבְעָֽה׃
records.gloss: And saw [the] sons of Benjamin that they were struck down. And gave [the] men of Israel place to Benjamin, for they trusted in the ambush which they had set against the Gibeah.
pieces: Then the Benjaminites saw that they were beaten. The men of Israel had given ground to Benjamin, because they were counting on the ambush they had set against Gibeah.

L.36: And the sons of Benjamin saw that they were struck down. And the men of Israel gave place to Benjamin, for they trusted in the ambush that they had set against Gibeah.

R.36: Then the men of Benjamin saw that they had lost. The Israelites had pulled back from them on purpose, because they were counting on the soldiers they had hidden near Gibeah.

decisions.choice: Benjamin saw that they were struck down: the end of the battle, told first
decisions.reason: The first sentence gives the end, when the Benjaminites saw they had lost (verse 41). The rest of the verse goes back to tell how it came about, starting with Israel's pretended retreat.

decisions.choice: gave place: gave way, pulled back
decisions.reason: To give place is to yield ground, here on purpose, so that the Benjaminites would follow them away from Gibeah (verse 32).

decisions.choice: trusted in the ambush: relied on it
decisions.reason: The verb means to trust or rely on. The tribes could fall back because they knew the hidden men would take the town behind the Benjaminites.

decisions.choice: had given ground (B); had pulled back ... on purpose (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable show by the tense that this happened before Benjamin saw its defeat (m1). Readable says why they pulled back.

records.source: וְהָאֹרֵ֣ב הֵחִ֔ישׁוּ וַֽיִּפְשְׁט֖וּ אֶל־הַגִּבְעָ֑ה וַיִּמְשֹׁךְ֙ הָאֹרֵ֔ב וַיַּ֥ךְ אֶת־כָּל־הָעִ֖יר לְפִי־חָֽרֶב׃
records.gloss: And the ambush hurried and rushed against the Gibeah, and moved on the ambush and struck all the city to [the] mouth of [the] sword.
pieces: The men in ambush moved quickly and rushed into Gibeah. They spread out and struck down the whole town with the sword.

L.37: And the ambush hurried and rushed against Gibeah, and the ambush moved on and struck the whole city with the edge of the sword.

R.37: The soldiers who had been hiding rushed quickly into Gibeah. They spread through the town and killed everyone in it with their swords.

decisions.choice: moved on: spread out through the town
decisions.reason: The verb means to draw out or march on. Here the ambush, once inside, spreads through Gibeah. The same verb is used of an army moving forward in 4:6.

decisions.choice: struck the whole city with the edge of the sword
decisions.reason: As at 1:8: they killed the people of the town. The town's fighting men were away on the roads, so those killed were chiefly those left inside.

decisions.choice: the men in ambush (B); the soldiers who had been hiding (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew uses one word, "the ambush", for the hidden men. Balanced and Readable speak of the men.

records.source: וְהַמּוֹעֵ֗ד הָיָ֛ה לְאִ֥ישׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל עִם־הָאֹרֵ֑ב הֶ֕רֶב לְהַעֲלוֹתָ֛ם מַשְׂאַ֥ת הֶעָשָׁ֖ן מִן־הָעִֽיר׃
records.gloss: And the appointed sign was to [the] men of Israel with the ambush: make great their causing to go up [a] rising of the smoke from the city.
pieces: The men of Israel had agreed on a signal with the men in ambush: they were to send up a great cloud of smoke from the town.

L.38: And the appointed sign that the men of Israel had with the ambush was [this]: make great their sending up of a rising of smoke from the city.

R.38: The Israelite army and the hidden soldiers had agreed on a signal. When the soldiers had taken the town, they would make a large cloud of smoke rise from it.

decisions.choice: the appointed sign: a signal agreed beforehand
decisions.reason: The word means an appointed time or place, here an agreed signal. The smoke would tell the main army to turn and fight (verses 39-40), as the smoke of Ai did in Joshua 8:20-21.

decisions.choice: make great their sending up: the Hebrew is hard to read here
decisions.reason: The Hebrew reads awkwardly, as if "make great" were a command inside the description of the sign. It most likely means they were to make a great column of smoke rise. A word may have dropped out of the text.

decisions.choice: a rising of smoke: a column of smoke
decisions.reason: The word for "rising" is used of a signal fire or column of smoke that goes up (Jeremiah 6:1). Verse 40 calls it "a pillar of smoke".

decisions.choice: When the soldiers had taken the town
decisions.reason: Readable says when the signal was to be given, as verses 37 and 40 show.

records.source: וַיַּהֲפֹ֥ךְ אִֽישׁ־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בַּמִּלְחָמָ֑ה וּבִנְיָמִ֡ן הֵחֵל֩ לְהַכּ֨וֹת חֲלָלִ֤ים בְּאִֽישׁ־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ כִּשְׁלֹשִׁ֣ים אִ֔ישׁ כִּ֣י אָמְר֔וּ אַךְ֩ נִגּ֨וֹף נִגָּ֥ף הוּא֙ לְפָנֵ֔ינוּ כַּמִּלְחָמָ֖ה הָרִאשֹׁנָֽה׃
records.gloss: And turned [the] men of Israel in the battle. And Benjamin had begun to strike slain among [the] men of Israel, about thirty man, for they said, Surely struck down, struck down [is] he before us, as the battle the first.
pieces: Then the men of Israel turned around in the battle. Benjamin had already started cutting down the men of Israel and had killed about thirty of them, and they said, "They are surely beaten by us, as in the first battle."

L.39: And the men of Israel turned in the battle. And Benjamin had begun to strike [some] slain among the men of Israel, about thirty men, for they said, "Surely he is utterly struck down before us, as [in] the first battle."

R.39: Then the men of Israel turned back to fight. The men of Benjamin had already begun to kill some of them, about thirty men. They said, "We are surely beating them, just as we did in the first battle."

decisions.choice: the men of Israel turned in the battle: they stopped retreating and faced Benjamin
decisions.reason: The verb means to turn round. Up to now the tribes had been pretending to flee; at the signal they turned and fought. Verse 41 tells the same turn again, at the moment Benjamin saw the smoke.

decisions.choice: Benjamin had begun to strike: what happened before the turn, as in verse 31
decisions.reason: This repeats verses 31-32 to explain why Benjamin pressed on: they had killed about thirty men and believed they were winning again.

decisions.choice: surely struck down, struck down: the doubled verb for certainty
decisions.reason: Hebrew repeats a verb to stress it. The Benjaminites are sure the tribes are beaten.

decisions.choice: They are surely beaten by us (B); We are surely beating them (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "he" for Israel as one man. Balanced and Readable say "they" or "them".

records.source: וְהַמַּשְׂאֵ֗ת הֵחֵ֛לָּה לַעֲל֥וֹת מִן־הָעִ֖יר עַמּ֣וּד עָשָׁ֑ן וַיִּ֤פֶן בִּנְיָמִן֙ אַחֲרָ֔יו וְהִנֵּ֛ה עָלָ֥ה כְלִיל־הָעִ֖יר הַשָּׁמָֽיְמָה׃
records.gloss: And the rising began to go up from the city, [a] pillar of smoke, and turned Benjamin behind him, and look, went up [the] whole of the city to the heavens.
pieces: But when the signal began to rise from the town in a column of smoke, the Benjaminites looked behind them, and there was the whole town going up in smoke to the sky.

L.40: And the rising began to go up from the city, a pillar of smoke, and Benjamin turned behind him, and look, the whole of the city was going up to the heavens.

R.40: Then the signal of smoke began to rise from the town like a pillar. The men of Benjamin looked back and saw the whole town burning, with smoke rising up to the sky.

decisions.choice: the whole of the city: the town going up as a whole offering
decisions.reason: The word for "whole" is also used of an offering burned completely on the altar. The law commands that a town in Israel that turns to other gods be burned as a whole offering to the LORD (Deuteronomy 13:17); Gibeah is treated like such a town. The same picture is used of Ai (Joshua 8:20).

decisions.choice: turned behind him, and look: the story shows what the Benjaminites saw
decisions.reason: "Look" puts the reader where the Benjaminites stood, turning to see their town in smoke.

decisions.choice: the signal ... in a column of smoke (B); the signal of smoke ... like a pillar (R)
decisions.reason: "The rising" is the agreed signal of verse 38, so Balanced and Readable call it the signal.

records.source: וְאִ֤ישׁ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ הָפַ֔ךְ וַיִּבָּהֵ֖ל אִ֣ישׁ בִּנְיָמִ֑ן כִּ֣י רָאָ֔ה כִּֽי־נָגְעָ֥ה עָלָ֖יו הָרָעָֽה׃
records.gloss: And [the] men of Israel turned, and were terrified [the] men of Benjamin, for he saw that had touched upon him the disaster.
pieces: Then the men of Israel turned to fight, and the men of Benjamin were terrified, because they saw that disaster had come upon them.

L.41: And the men of Israel turned, and the men of Benjamin were terrified, for they saw that the disaster had touched them.

R.41: Then the men of Israel turned to attack, and the men of Benjamin were terrified. They saw that disaster had come upon them.

decisions.choice: the disaster had touched them: what they did not know in verse 34
decisions.reason: Verse 34 said they did not know that disaster was about to reach them. Now they see it. The word is the one for the "evil" of Gibeah (verses 3, 12-13).

decisions.choice: terrified: struck with sudden fear and confusion
decisions.reason: The verb means to be dismayed or thrown into panic, as an army is when it sees it is lost (1 Samuel 28:21).

decisions.choice: they ... them
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "he saw" and "him" for the men of Benjamin as one body. Even Literal says "they" and "them" here, since English cannot use "he" after "the men of Benjamin".

records.source: וַיִּפְנ֞וּ לִפְנֵ֨י אִ֤ישׁ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ אֶל־דֶּ֣רֶךְ הַמִּדְבָּ֔ר וְהַמִּלְחָמָ֖ה הִדְבִּיקָ֑תְהוּ וַאֲשֶׁר֙ מֵהֶ֣עָרִ֔ים מַשְׁחִיתִ֥ים אוֹת֖וֹ בְּתוֹכֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And they turned before [the] men of Israel to [the] way of the wilderness, and the battle overtook him, and [those] who [were] from the cities [were] destroying him in its midst.
pieces: So they turned and fled from the men of Israel toward the wilderness, but they could not escape the fighting, and those who came out of the towns cut them down in the middle of it.

L.42: And they turned before the men of Israel toward the way of the wilderness, but the battle overtook them, and those who [were] from the cities were destroying them in its midst.

R.42: So they ran from the men of Israel toward the wilderness. But they could not escape the battle. Israelite soldiers came out of the towns and killed them there between the two armies.

decisions.choice: the battle overtook them: they could not get away from the fighting
decisions.reason: The battle is pictured as chasing and catching them. They fled, but the fighting came after them.

decisions.choice: those from the cities destroying them in its midst: the Hebrew is hard to follow
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "the cities", plural, and "in its midst". It most likely means the men of the ambush, coming out of Gibeah and other towns, caught the Benjaminites between them and the main army. A reading "the city", meaning Gibeah alone, would be smoother, but the Hebrew text has the plural.

decisions.choice: toward the wilderness: east, to the dry country toward the Jordan
decisions.reason: The wilderness here is the dry, rocky land east of Benjamin's towns, sloping down to the Jordan valley. It is where the survivors flee (verse 45).

decisions.choice: Israelite soldiers ... between the two armies
decisions.reason: Readable says who came out of the towns and what "in its midst" means (m2).

records.source: כִּתְּר֤וּ אֶת־בִּנְיָמִן֙ הִרְדִיפֻ֔הוּ מְנוּחָ֖ה הִדְרִיכֻ֑הוּ עַ֛ד נֹ֥כַח הַגִּבְעָ֖ה מִמִּזְרַח־שָֽׁמֶשׁ׃
records.gloss: They surrounded Benjamin, they pursued him; [at] resting place they trod him down, as far as opposite the Gibeah from [the] rising of [the] sun.
pieces: They surrounded the Benjaminites and chased them, and they trampled them down at Menuhah, as far as the area east of Gibeah.

L.43: They surrounded Benjamin, they pursued him; [at] Menuhah they trod him down, as far as opposite Gibeah toward the rising of the sun.

R.43: They surrounded the men of Benjamin and chased them. They crushed them at a place called Menuhah, as far as the area east of Gibeah.

decisions.choice: Menuhah: most likely a place name; it can also mean "rest" or "easily"
decisions.reason: The word means "rest" or "resting place". It may name a place, perhaps the clan town of Nohah in Benjamin (1 Chronicles 8:2). It may also mean they trampled them down "at their resting place", where they stopped, or "without effort". Some copies of the Greek translation read it as the place name Nohah.

decisions.choice: surrounded, pursued, trod down: three verbs without "and"
decisions.reason: The verbs are set side by side with no joining word, which makes the account quick and breathless.

decisions.choice: from the rising of the sun: on the east
decisions.reason: "The rising of the sun" means the east.

decisions.choice: at Menuhah
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable take the word as a place name (m1); Literal brackets "at" since the Hebrew has no preposition.

records.source: וַֽיִּפְּלוּ֙ מִבִּנְיָמִ֔ן שְׁמֹנָֽה־עָשָׂ֥ר אֶ֖לֶף אִ֑ישׁ אֶת־כָּל־אֵ֖לֶּה אַנְשֵׁי־חָֽיִל׃
records.gloss: And fell of Benjamin eighteen thousand man; all these [were] men of strength.
pieces: Of Benjamin 18,000 men fell, all of them brave warriors.

L.44: And there fell of Benjamin 18,000 men; all these [were] men of strength.

R.44: Of Benjamin's army 18,000 men were killed. All of them were brave soldiers.

decisions.choice: men of strength: able, brave warriors
decisions.reason: The phrase names men of strength, skill and courage in war (6:12; 11:1). It honors the fallen Benjaminites even in defeat.

decisions.choice: 18,000: the first part of the total
decisions.reason: Verses 44-45 add up to 25,000: 18,000 here, then 5,000 and 2,000 (verse 45), the round number of verse 46. On the size of the numbers see verse 2.

records.source: וַיִּפְנ֞וּ וַיָּנֻ֤סוּ הַמִּדְבָּ֨רָה֙ אֶל־סֶ֣לַע הָֽרִמּ֔וֹן וַיְעֹֽלְלֻ֨הוּ֙ בַּֽמְסִלּ֔וֹת חֲמֵ֥שֶׁת אֲלָפִ֖ים אִ֑ישׁ וַיַּדְבִּ֤יקוּ אַחֲרָיו֙ עַד־גִּדְעֹ֔ם וַיַּכּ֥וּ מִמֶּ֖נּוּ אַלְפַּ֥יִם אִֽישׁ׃
records.gloss: And they turned and fled to the wilderness, to [the] rock of the Rimmon. And they gleaned him on the highways, five thousand man; and they pursued closely after him to Gidom and they struck of him two thousand man.
pieces: Then they turned and ran toward the wilderness, to the rock of Rimmon. The Israelites picked off 5,000 men along the roads, and they kept after them as far as Gidom and killed 2,000 more.

L.45: And they turned and fled toward the wilderness, to the rock of Rimmon. And they gleaned them on the highways, 5,000 men, and they pursued hard after them as far as Gidom and struck 2,000 men of them.

R.45: The rest of Benjamin's men ran toward the wilderness, to the rock of Rimmon. The Israelites hunted down and killed 5,000 of them along the roads. They chased them as far as Gidom and killed 2,000 more.

decisions.choice: gleaned them: picked them off one by one
decisions.reason: Gleaning is gathering the grain or grapes left after the harvest (Leviticus 19:9-10; 8:2). The picture is of the tribes catching the stragglers, the last ones left, along the roads.

decisions.choice: the rock of Rimmon; Gidom: places east of Gibeah
decisions.reason: The rock of Rimmon was a high crag or cliff, most likely near the town of Rimmon east of Bethel, a hard place to attack. Gidom is not known today.

decisions.choice: The Israelites
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "they"; Balanced and Readable say who did the killing, since the subject changes from Benjamin to Israel.

records.source: וַיְהִי֩ כָל־הַנֹּ֨פְלִ֜ים מִבִּנְיָמִ֗ן עֶשְׂרִים֩ וַחֲמִשָּׁ֨ה אֶ֥לֶף אִ֛ישׁ שֹׁ֥לֵֽף חֶ֖רֶב בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֑וּא אֶֽת־כָּל־אֵ֖לֶּה אַנְשֵׁי־חָֽיִל׃
records.gloss: And were all those fallen of Benjamin twenty and five thousand man drawing [the] sword on the day the that; all these [were] men of strength.
pieces: So in all 25,000 men of Benjamin who were armed with swords fell that day, all of them brave warriors.

L.46: And all who fell of Benjamin were 25,000 men drawing [the] sword on that day; all these [were] men of strength.

R.46: That day 25,000 of Benjamin's soldiers were killed. All of them were brave men who fought with swords.

decisions.choice: 25,000: the round total of verse 35's 25,100
decisions.reason: Verse 35 gives the exact number, 25,100; this verse rounds it, as the sum of verses 44-45 (18,000, 5,000, 2,000) does. On the size of the numbers see verse 2.

decisions.choice: men of strength
decisions.reason: As in verse 44.

decisions.choice: drawing [the] sword (L); armed with swords (B); who fought with swords (R)
decisions.reason: As in verse 2.

records.source: וַיִּפְנ֞וּ וַיָּנֻ֤סוּ הַמִּדְבָּ֨רָה֙ אֶל־סֶ֣לַע הָֽרִמּ֔וֹן שֵׁ֥שׁ מֵא֖וֹת אִ֑ישׁ וַיֵּֽשְׁבוּ֙ בְּסֶ֣לַע רִמּ֔וֹן אַרְבָּעָ֖ה חֳדָשִֽׁים׃
records.gloss: And turned and fled to the wilderness, to [the] rock of the Rimmon, six hundred man, and they stayed at [the] rock of Rimmon four months.
pieces: But 600 men turned and escaped into the wilderness to the rock of Rimmon, and they stayed there four months.

L.47: But 600 men turned and fled toward the wilderness, to the rock of Rimmon, and they stayed at the rock of Rimmon four months.

R.47: But 600 men escaped into the wilderness to the rock of Rimmon. They stayed there for four months.

decisions.choice: 600 men: all that was left of Benjamin
decisions.reason: These 600 are the tribe's only survivors. Chapter 21 tells how the tribes, grieving that one tribe was about to be lost, found wives for them (21:6-7, 13).

decisions.choice: they stayed at the rock four months: a stronghold that could not easily be taken
decisions.reason: The crag gave the survivors a safe place to hold out until the tribes sent word of peace to them (21:13).

decisions.choice: there
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "there" for the second "rock of Rimmon"; Literal repeats the name as the Hebrew does.

records.source: וְאִ֨ישׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל שָׁ֣בוּ אֶל־בְּנֵ֤י בִנְיָמִן֙ וַיַּכּ֣וּם לְפִי־חֶ֔רֶב מֵעִ֤יר מְתֹם֙ עַד־בְּהֵמָ֔ה עַ֖ד כָּל־הַנִּמְצָ֑א גַּ֛ם כָּל־הֶעָרִ֥ים הַנִּמְצָא֖וֹת שִׁלְּח֥וּ בָאֵֽשׁ׃פ
records.gloss: And [the] men of Israel turned back to [the] sons of Benjamin, and struck them to [the] mouth of [the] sword, from [the] city, entire, to [the] beast, to all that was found; also all the cities that were found they sent in the fire.
pieces: Then the men of Israel turned back against the Benjaminites and struck them down with the sword, from the people of the towns to the animals, everything they found. They also set on fire every town they came to.

L.48: And the men of Israel turned back against the sons of Benjamin and struck them with the edge of the sword, from the entire city to the beasts, to everything that was found; also all the cities that were found they set on fire.

R.48: Then the men of Israel went back to the towns of Benjamin. They killed the people and the animals, everything they found. They burned every town they came to.

decisions.choice: the entire city: the Hebrew text; some copies read "the men of the city"
alternatives: from the men of the city to the beasts
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word means "soundness" or "entire", giving "from the entire city". A few Hebrew copies have a word that differs by one vowel and means "men", giving "from the men of the city to the beasts", which fits the list better. The meaning is much the same: everyone in the towns.

decisions.choice: they struck ... and set the cities on fire: Benjamin treated like a town devoted to destruction
decisions.reason: The tribes do to Benjamin's towns what the law commands for a town in Israel that serves other gods: kill its people and animals with the sword and burn it (Deuteronomy 13:16-17). The story tells it without approval; chapter 21 shows the tribes grieving over what they had done (21:2-3, 6, 15).

decisions.choice: struck them with the edge of the sword
decisions.reason: As at verse 37 and 1:8: they killed them.

decisions.choice: from the people of the towns to the animals (B); the people and the animals (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say whom the word "city" stands for here: everyone in the towns (m1).
